territorial_scope.description: Applies to the protection of children and adolescents in digital environments in Colombia, with obligations on national government bodies and actors operating in the country.

evidence.quote: entornos digitales sanos y seguros para los niños, niñas y adolescentes del país

summary.short: Colombian statute (Law 2489 of 2025) that sets duties for the government, digital service and software providers, telecom industry, schools and parents to promote healthy and safe digital environments for children and adolescents. In force from publication; regulation due within six months.
summary.long: Law 2489 of 2025 sets principles and duties to promote healthy and safe digital environments for children and adolescents in Colombia (Arts. 1-3). The national government must adopt measures against online violence, exploitation, discrimination and harmful content, require digital service providers to cooperate, and recognise parental control tools, age-classification notices and age-verification mechanisms (Art. 4). The Ministry of ICT must set policies on safe use of ICT in coordination with the Communications Regulation Commission and run awareness programmes (Art. 5). The Ministry of Education must set curriculum guidelines on digital citizenship and privacy (Art. 6), and schools must run workshops for parents (Art. 7, par. 2). The law creates a National Committee on Technology, Childhood and Adolescence that meets at least once a year (Art. 7). Parents and caregivers receive responsibilities (Art. 8), the software industry must protect children and design software ethically (Art. 9), and the ICT Law gains a funding function (Art. 10). Ministries must submit annual reports (Art. 11), consolidate an open-resource repository (Art. 12), and establish an integrated monitoring and evaluation system that must respect children's privacy and oversee telecom industry use of secure-design guidelines (Art. 13). Regulation is due within six months of entry into force (Art. 14). The law takes effect on publication (Art. 15) and contains no sanction provisions.

relations.target_text: Ley 1341 de 2009, art. 35 (Ley de TIC; Art. 10 adds a new numeral 24 to art. 35)
relations.note: Adds a new numeral 24 to art. 35 of Ley 1341 de 2009 on financing education and awareness programmes for a healthy digital environment. Art. 5(2) separately refers to the competences under Ley 1341 de 2009 as modified by Ley 1978 de 2019.

evidence.quote: Adiciónese un numeral nuevo al artículo 35 de la Ley 1341 de 2009

relations.note: Art. 5(2) assigns the Ministry policy and regulation powers 'atendiendo las competencias previstas en la Ley 1341 de 2009 modificada por la Ley 1978 de 2019'.

evidence.quote: atendiendo las competencias previstas en la Ley 1341 de 2009 modificada por la Ley 1978 de 2019

relations.note: Art. 7 includes one representative of the Comité Nacional Interinstitucional 'del que trata la Ley 1336 de 2009' in the National Committee on Technology, Childhood and Adolescence.

evidence.quote: un representante del Comité Nacional Interinstitucional del que trata la Ley 1336 de 2009

relations.note: Art. 7 Parágrafo 1 requires the Technology and Childhood Committee to meet with the anti-trafficking committee defined in art. 12 of Ley 985 de 2005. Art. 13 Parágrafo requires the monitoring system to be linked to the national trafficking information system described in art. 17 of Ley 985 de 2005.

evidence.quote: deberá articularse con el Sistema Nacional de Información sobre la Trata de Personas descrito en el artículo 17 de la Ley 985 de 2005

relations.note: Art. 3 (principle of best interests of children) cites art. 44 of the Constitución Política as its constitutional basis.

evidence.quote: De conformidad con el artículo 44 de la Constitución Política

relations.target_text: Código de Infancia y Adolescencia, art. 8
relations.note: Art. 3 (best interests of children principle) refers to art. 8 of the Código de Infancia y Adolescencia. The document does not give that code's law number.

evidence.quote: el artículo 8o del Código de Infancia y Adolescencia

relations.target_text: Convención de los Derechos del Niño; Observaciones Generales núm. 25 and núm. 16 (UN Committee on the Rights of the Child)
relations.note: Art. 4 states that the children's rights in the law apply complementarily to the Convention on the Rights of the Child and General Comments no. 25 (digital environment) and no. 16 (business sector and children's rights).

evidence.quote: según lo dispone la Convención de los Derechos del Niño

relations.target_text: All provisions contrary to this law (not identified by name)
relations.note: General repeal clause. The text names no specific instrument or article it repeals.

evidence.quote: deroga todas las disposiciones que le sean contrarias

notes: Only one repeal is stated, and it is general: Art. 15 repeals unnamed contrary provisions, so no specific instrument is repealed. The document does not state the bill that enacted the law; it shows only the signatures, the adoption date (17 July 2025) and the Diario Oficial publication (No. 53.185, 18 July 2025). The header also says the Diario Oficial was available online on 19 July 2025; this is publication metadata, not a text provision. Art. 7 lists 'la Policía Nacional' twice in the composition of the Committee. Art. 7 (annual meeting) and Art. 7 Parágrafo 1 (meeting once per semester with the anti-trafficking committee) set different meeting frequencies for different bodies; they are not in conflict. Art. 14 requires regulation within six months of entry into force, while Art. 15 says the law takes effect on publication. Target instrument IDs are left empty because none of the cited instruments is identified in the registry. The document includes an editorial compilation notice from Avance Jurídico, which is not part of the law.
